title: A fatal flaw overrides a strong score
source: Technically this is an 8/10: the evaluation is unusually rigorous. However, the Methods explicitly say patient consent was not obtained. That weakness alone makes me recommend rejection.
pressure: Opinion and score have different sets of supporting findings. A high rating and rejection must not be forced into agreement.
rule: Opinion.supported_by is optional. Here it points to the decisive ethics weakness; the technical score points to the strength. Neither support list is inferred from the other.

opinion.summary: Technically strong, but the consent issue is decisive.

decision.rationale: The lack of patient consent is decisive.

weaknesses.text: The Methods state that patient consent was not obtained.

title: A score and confidence, with no prose
pressure: A strict hierarchy could tempt an importer to invent findings that explain a score, or treat confidence as a finding-derived judgment.
rule: Keep both original answers and their definitions. supported_by is absent. Confidence is a source-stated answer, not a computed probability or an inferred finding.

title: A purely qualitative review
source: I recommend acceptance. The proof is elegant and the exposition is clear. Please define the symbol in Equation 2.
pressure: There are no numerical scores, no extracted claims and no performed checks. The requested edit is not explicitly tied to a weakness.
rule: Metrics and lower-layer objects remain optional. Preserve two strengths and a standalone change; do not invent a weakness or a score.

opinion.summary: Accept: elegant proof and clear exposition.

title: One claim, conflicting observations
source: The paper claims cross-campus generalization. Its original evaluation uses one campus. An additional replication covers two campuses, but both are in the same climate. Generalization is still only partially established.
pressure: Evidence has mixed implications. A pointer alone cannot label which observation supports or limits the claim.
rule: The finding states the synthesis and its limitations. about can include one claim and multiple check results. Evidence pointers remain plain; no signed evidence edges are needed.

results.text: Replication: two campuses in one climate.

weaknesses.text: The replication broadens site coverage, but a single climate still limits the generalization claim.

title: The checker fails, not the work
source: The reproduction runner exhausted its GPU quota before any experiment began. I cannot assess reproducibility from this attempt.
pressure: Execution failure can be mistaken for a failed scientific result or a quality score of zero.
rule: Record the failed examination and unassessed observation. Do not infer a weakness, rejection or zero reproducibility score.

procedure.description: Attempt to run the supplied experiments.

results.text: Runner exhausted its GPU quota before experiment start.

title: Raw counts with no evaluative score
source: Reference checker: 80 references inspected, 3 unresolved. Elapsed time: 12.4 seconds. No reviewer judgment was supplied.
pressure: Counts and runtime are measurements, but they are not numerical summaries of evaluative findings. The strict hierarchy cannot treat every number as an overall metric.
rule: Keep raw quantities and their units in result.data once. Metrics are summaries or overall assessment scores; do not manufacture findings or an overall rating from checker output.

title: Alternative remedies and a conditional decision
source: Accept only if the authors either remove the causal claim OR run a randomized study. Doing either is sufficient; both are not required.
pressure: Two independent change records could accidentally imply that both actions are required. A revision enum alone cannot express the decision condition.
rule: The Changes description requires alternative remedies to stay together in one item when either remedy is sufficient. Preserve the decision condition in rationale. No extra schema construct is needed.

decision.rationale: Acceptance is conditional on either removing the causal claim OR running a randomized study; either is sufficient.

weaknesses.text: The causal claim is not established by the current design.

changes.text: Either remove the causal claim OR run a randomized study; either remedy is sufficient.

title: A score for package A versus package B
source: Code package A: usability 8/10. Code package B: usability 2/10. Overall paper: 6/10. Both package scores use the same rubric.
pressure: This only concerns separately scoring individual artifacts. The same rubric produces 8 for A and 2 for B; without a subject reference, a structured score cannot say which package it evaluates. Normal overall review scores do not have this ambiguity.
rule: The current metric layer is for overall summaries. Preserve the per-package ratings in the original source or finding text; do not invent checks or duplicate rubric definitions to force them into that layer. No subject field is added in this version.
preserve_unmapped: Both artifact-local ratings are retained in finding text. They are outside the current structured overall-summary metric layer.

title: The same check changes across versions
source: Package revision abc failed installation. After the authors supplied revision def, installation succeeded. The review concerns paper v2; I am no longer requesting an installation fix.
pressure: A flat failed status or stale change can wrongly imply that the current package is still broken.
rule: Keep two observations with the exact artifact versions in their pointers. Preserve the final comment; do not emit an active requested change when the reviewer says it is no longer requested.

comments.text: Installation succeeds in revision def; the earlier request is no longer active.

title: A multi-step argument within one finding
source: The train/test split leaks patient identities. Consequently the reported accuracy is inflated; consequently the clinical deployment claim is unsupported.
pressure: The source gives a multi-step argument, but that does not require a separate graph node for every step.
rule: Preserve the argument in the text of one substantive finding. There are no finding-to-finding support links in this version.

claims.text: The model is ready for clinical deployment.

weaknesses.text: Patient-identity leakage inflates the accuracy estimate, so it does not establish the clinical deployment claim.

title: An absence claim without a performed check
source: The paper does not explain how missing data were handled. Please add that explanation. I did not inspect the code.
pressure: An importer might manufacture a code check or evidence of nonexistent text to justify a missing-information finding.
rule: Keep the reviewer’s stated weakness and a change addressing it. A pointer to the relevant Methods section is optional context; no code check or fake quotation is required.

weaknesses.text: The paper does not explain how missing data were handled.

changes.text: Explain how missing data were handled.

title: One paragraph contains all five kinds of point
source: The dataset is unusually broad, but the subgroup counts are small. How were the thresholds selected? I use robustness here to mean stability across random seeds. To address the small subgroup counts, please report per-group intervals.
pressure: A heading or paragraph can mix praise, criticism, a question, a neutral clarification and a requested action. Reusing fields must not flatten those distinctions.
rule: Keep five separate collections under findings. Classify each source point once; the change can address the weakness without being duplicated as another weakness.

comments.text: I use robustness here to mean stability across random seeds.

title: One uncertainty type, two contexts
source: My probability that the split leaks patient identities is 0.6, and my confidence in assigning that probability is 0.8. Taking this concern into account, my overall score is 7/10, with a plausible range of 6–8 and confidence of 0.7 in that score.
pressure: A probability about an assertion and a range of score values are different quantities, even though their surrounding uncertainty fields can be reused.
rule: Use one Uncertainty definition: probability on the finding, interval on the metric, and optional credence/rationale on either. Do not put both probability and interval in one object, or substitute model extraction confidence for reviewer uncertainty.

weaknesses.text: The split may leak patient identities.

title: An exact span after an emoji and a line break
source: Paper text: “🧪 Trial\nThe effect is robust.\n”. Reviewer: “The robustness claim is too strong for this small sample.”
pressure: An emoji occupies one Unicode code point but two UTF-16 code units. PDF extraction, normalization and page-relative counting can otherwise shift the selected passage.
rule: Identify the exact extracted text with text_ref. Use zero-based Unicode code-point offsets [start, end), counting stored whitespace. Page and section remain descriptive locators; quote matches the selected slice. No span is inferred without access to the referenced text.

weaknesses.text: The robustness claim is too strong for this small sample.
